states.name: Oregon
states.permitNotice: Oregon generally requires a Waterway Access Permit for non-motorized boats. Exemptions apply on some trips, so check the current Marine Board rules.

states.name: Washington
states.permitNotice: Washington generally requires a Discover Pass to park at state-managed launches (WDFW, State Parks and DNR); a WDFW Vehicle Access Pass covers WDFW sites only. Federal, county, city and utility launches set their own fees.

states.name: Utah
states.permitNotice: Many Utah river trips need a federal permit: Dinosaur NM (NPS), Desolation/Gray Canyons, Westwater Canyon, the San Juan and Labyrinth Canyon (BLM) and Canyonlands (NPS). Most permits are booked on Recreation.gov. Some launches charge fees. Check the managing agency before you go.

states.name: Arizona
states.permitNotice: Several Arizona river trips need a permit. The Grand Canyon (Lees Ferry or Diamond Creek) needs a National Park Service river permit, and the Hualapai Tribe charges fees to use Diamond Creek. The Upper Salt (Mar 1 to May 15) needs a Tonto National Forest permit plus a White Mountain Apache permit. Lower Salt and Verde sites on the Tonto may need a Tonto Pass. Many permits are booked on Recreation.gov. Check the managing agency before you go.

states.name: Colorado
states.permitNotice: Some Colorado river trips need a permit or pass: Dinosaur NM (NPS; including a one-day play permit to take out at Deerlodge after floating from upstream), Gunnison Gorge Wilderness and Ruby-Horsethief overnight camping (BLM), self-issued DENCA overnight permits, and CPW State Parks passes (including Arkansas Headwaters fee sites). Some launches charge fees. Check the managing agency before you go.

states.name: Wyoming
states.permitNotice: Some Wyoming float trips need a permit, pass or inspection: every watercraft entering Wyoming from March 1 to November 30 needs an aquatic invasive species inspection. State AIS decals are also required unless the craft is exempt; check the agency rules. Grand Teton National Park requires a park boat permit; the Snake River from the Hoback confluence through the canyon is a Forest Service fee area with group permits; the Wind River Indian Reservation (Wind River Canyon and the river below Dubois) requires tribal permits and Inter-Tribal Council approval for rafting. Wyoming streambeds next to private land are private: float through, but do not anchor, wade or get out without permission. Check the managing agency before you go.

states.name: California
states.agency: California State Parks Division of Boating and Waterways
states.intro: Explore the Russian River near Forestville, the Lower American near Sacramento, and the South Fork American around Coloma and Lotus. Compare sourced access maps, available USGS reference readings and published seasonal guidance where available. Exact landings and general access areas are labelled separately.
states.description: Plan Russian River, Lower American and South Fork American floats in California with sourced access maps, reference gauges and available trip-time guidance.

states.name: Missouri
states.permitNotice: Most Missouri floats need no permit, but rules apply: state law bans glass beverage containers on canoes, kayaks and tubes, requires food and drink in a sealed non-glass cooler and a closable trash bag affixed to the boat, and requires children under 7 to wear a life jacket. On the Current and Jacks Fork (Ozark National Scenic Riverways) the park closes the rivers during floods and sets motor horsepower limits; the Eleven Point (Mark Twain National Forest) has a 25 hp limit and no glass. There is no general right to cross private land: banks and gravel bars beside private land may be private, so launch and take out only at public accesses. Check the managing agency before you go.

states.name: Arkansas
states.permitNotice: Most Arkansas floats need no permit, but rules apply: state law bans glass containers in canoes, kayaks and tubes, requires food and drink in sealed containers, a closable trash bag affixed to the boat and floating drink holders, and requires children 12 and under to wear a life jacket. On the Buffalo National River the park also bans Styrofoam and flotillas of three or more boats, and limits motors below Erbie Ford. Below Bull Shoals, Norfork, Beaver and Greers Ferry dams the water rises fast during power generation — check the release schedule. The Illinois River in Oklahoma needs a GRDA float permit. Banks and gravel bars beside private land may be private, so launch and take out only at public accesses. Check the managing agency before you go.

states.name: Wisconsin
states.permitNotice: Use public access sites or obtain permission to cross private land. Wisconsin’s navigable-water rules do not grant general access across private banks. Launch fees and local rules vary. Many rivers have dams; a listed section is not assurance of an open portage. Check the managing agency before you go.
states.intro: Explore the Kickapoo, Bois Brule, Namekagon, St. Croix, Flambeau and Wisconsin rivers. Compare sourced access areas, current gauge readings where available, and agency-published trip times. Sections with unresolved access or dam crossings remain under review.
states.description: Explore Wisconsin river access maps on the Kickapoo, Bois Brule, Namekagon, St. Croix and more, with available USGS readings and published guide times.

states.name: Minnesota
states.intro: Explore Minnesota paddles on the Kettle, Pine, Root, Cannon, Straight, Rum, Zumbro, Crow Wing and Mississippi rivers. Compare shorter outings, full-day trips, public access maps and published guidance. Exact landing pins and approximate access areas are labelled separately.
states.description: Plan Minnesota river trips with public access maps, dotted river-course overviews, published trip guidance and available reference flow.
states.permitNotice: Check Minnesota watercraft registration requirements for your boat. Non-motorized boats 10 feet or shorter are exempt; qualifying visiting boats also have exemptions. Parking and access restrictions vary by site. Check current agency notices before your trip.

rivers.gaugeName: Colorado River above Diamond Creek near Peach Springs, AZ
rivers.blurb: Lower Gorge of the Grand Canyon from Diamond Creek (Hualapai land) to Pearce Ferry in Lake Mead NRA. NPS Diamond Creek permit required.

sections.notes: NPS: 'It includes 52 river miles of smooth and white water'; noncommercial trips from Diamond Creek (river mile 225) 'take 2 to 5 days'. NPS Diamond Creek permit required; Hualapai Tribe fees to launch at Diamond Creek. Take out at Pearce Ferry or South Cove; the Pearce Ferry ramp is for river-trip take-outs only (NPS Lake Mead).

rivers.blurb: Dam-release tubing and kayaking reach below Saguaro Lake in the Tonto National Forest. Flow depends on releases from Stewart Mountain Dam. Tonto Pass required at the sites.

sections.takeOut: Blue Point Day Use Area (Lower Salt)

The reach sits below Stewart Mountain Dam, so check USGS 09502000 before going.

rivers.name: Clearwater River
rivers.blurb: Big, warm, summer water from Orofino toward Lewiston. A North Idaho alternative to the crowded Greenbelt.

sections.notes: Wide river, easy current. Jet boats and fishing traffic on weekends.
Longer valley miles into the Lewiston area. Wind can come up the canyon in the afternoon.

rivers.name: Henry's Fork (Ashton)
rivers.blurb: Choose named floats above Ashton Dam, Ora and Vernon floats ending above Chester Dam, or the separate Chester downstream ramp to Fun Farm float. Dam crossings are not included; older ambiguous itineraries remain under review.

sections.notes: Start at Stone Bridge, below the Warm River confluence, and finish at the Jump Off Canyon ramp on Fishermans Drive. Arrange the shuttle and inspect the takeout before launching.

rivers.blurb: A popular spring-fed water trail near Island Park, from the hand-carry launch at the old railroad trestle to the public Forest Service takeout above Mack’s Inn. Keep the public takeout distinct from private bridge-side landings.

sections.takeOut: Big Springs Water Trail Public Takeout
sections.notes: A spring-fed meadow float for hand-carried boats. Launch at the trestle-side water-trail facility and finish at the designated public takeout upstream of Mack’s Inn bridge. Arrange your shuttle and identify the clearing before launching; private resort and cabin landings are different sites.

rivers.name: Henry's Fork (Box Canyon)
rivers.blurb: Island Park Dam to Last Chance — a short basalt canyon on some of the most famous trout water in the West.

sections.notes: Launch at the Box Canyon boat ramp below Island Park Dam and take out at Last Chance. This is rocky moving water; releases and low water change the trip. Give wading anglers room and confirm the takeout before starting. Check current access and fishing rules before extending beyond Last Chance.

rivers.name: Lochsa River
rivers.blurb: Highway 12 whitewater. A spring Class III–IV that is over by the time the rest of Idaho is just warming up.

sections.notes: Peak is May–June. Not a tube float. USGS stage at this gauge is not the Lowell Bridge staff — check Lochsa.info for the boater gauge.
Packed rapids to the Selway confluence. Miss the takeout and you are on the Clearwater.

rivers.name: North Fork Payette (Cabarton)
rivers.blurb: The Cabarton whitewater run ends at Smiths Ferry. It is distinct from the advanced lower North Fork canyon toward Banks.

sections.notes: The Cabarton run ends at Smiths Ferry. BLM's NF02 guide shows Class III rapids including Howard’s Plunge (III+). The separate lower North Fork canyon toward Banks is advanced whitewater; it is not part of this trip.
sections.accessReview: BLM identifies both Cabarton Bridge and Smiths Ferry access as private. Current permission, operating arrangements and exact landing locations still need confirmation. This corrected reach is held for access review.

rivers.name: Payette River (Banks)
rivers.blurb: Idaho's closest commercial whitewater to Boise. Banks to Horseshoe Bend — waves, holes, and a highway shuttle.

sections.notes: BLM’s P02 guide measures this run from Banks River Access to Beehive Bend at 7.3 miles and includes Class III+ rapids. Arrange a road shuttle along Highway 55; confirm the current river-access fee and conditions.

sections.accessReview: The legacy takeout label does not establish whether it means the Parnell Recreation Site or the separate Horseshoe Dam Bridge access in BLM guide P03. Confirm the intended landing and route before planning.

rivers.name: Salmon River (Riggins)
rivers.blurb: Lower Salmon country. Day floats past Riggins, or the multi-day Hammer Creek to Heller Bar desert canyon.

sections.notes: Town-to-town. Warm water in summer, jet boats possible. Time Zone Rapid is the named drop.
The Lower Salmon. Typically 3–4 days. Snowhole is the big rapid. BLM camps, rattlesnakes, and a serious shuttle.

rivers.name: Salmon River (Salmon)
rivers.blurb: The River of No Return at town scale — Salmon to North Fork is a big, friendly Class I–II day.

sections.notes: Highway 93 shuttle. Big water, easy gradient. North Fork is where the Middle Fork comes in and the wilderness section begins.

rivers.name: Selway River (Permit)
rivers.blurb: Idaho's other permit-lottery classic. 47 canyon miles, one launch a day, no cell service.

sections.notes: Forest Service permit required. Typically 4–5 days in May–July. Moose Creek is midway. Portage or scout Selway Falls at the end.

rivers.name: South Fork Payette
rivers.gaugeName: South Fork Payette River at Lowman
rivers.blurb: Canyon water out of Lowman — hot springs on the bank, Swirly Canyon in the middle, Garden Valley at the bottom.

sections.notes: The Kirkham/Lowman to Deadwood area includes Class III+ rapids in BLM guide SF02. Staircase is much farther downstream, between Garden Valley and Banks; it is not above Lowman.
sections.accessReview: Kirkham and Lowman are different launch locations. The former six-mile listing combined them; a specific legal landing and matching distance must be established before enabling this trip.

sections.notes: BLM guide SF04 covers 8.6 miles from Danskin to Alder Creek; SF05 adds 4.4 miles from Alder Creek to Confluence. Stop at the Garden Valley/Middle Fork confluence access. Continuing to Banks enters the more difficult Staircase run.

distanceEvidence.note: Sum of contiguous BLM guide lengths: SF04 8.6 miles plus SF05 4.4 miles. This is a guide length, not a GPS trace.

sections.notes: A long canyon float. Fullmer at river mile 28 provides an intermediate public ramp; arrange your shuttle and allow time for stops. Use designated camps and the required overnight permit if breaking the trip over multiple days.

sections.notes: Upper-ish Joe. Wood and cold water. Best in early summer before it drops.
Flatter miles into the lake country. Watch for motorboats near town.

rivers.name: Rock Creek (Clinton)
rivers.blurb: Blue-ribbon creek east of Missoula with fast water and wood hazards. Seasonal boat-fishing restrictions and access closures require planning.

sections.notes: The Dalles boulder garden requires scouting for wood. FWP prohibits fishing from boats or vessels July 1–November 30; this is a fishing restriction, not a blanket prohibition on floating.

rivers.name: Smith River (Permit)
rivers.gaugeName: Smith bl Eagle Creek nr Fort Logan
rivers.blurb: Montana's only permit-lottery river. 59 canyon miles, 4–5 days, zero cell service.

sections.notes: Launch requires an FWP permit. Below ~150 cfs expect to drag boats.

rivers.name: Swan River
rivers.blurb: Quiet valley float into Bigfork. Take out above the Wild Mile unless you meant to run Class III.

sections.notes: Mellow until town. The Wild Mile gorge at Bigfork is a separate Class III run — don't float into it by accident.

rivers.name: Yellowstone River (Gardiner)
rivers.blurb: Whitewater stretch out of the Park boundary. Rafts and experienced paddlers.

sections.notes: Continuous wave trains at higher flows. Not a tube float.
sections.accessReview: A suitable launch at Queen of the Waters and the intended Corwin Springs landing have not been confirmed for this listing.

notices.text: FWP’s site linked from the older Corwin Springs map is now named Brogan’s Landing. Its current record still lists a flood-related emergency closure effective July 1, 2022 until further notice. Do not use that old map or the tourism listing as proof of an open boat launch.

rivers.blurb: Portland-area summer floats below Estacada, with a quieter upper run and a busy Barton-to-Carver tube stretch on hot weekends.

sections.notes: The quieter of the two listed floats. Cold water and moving current still demand a properly fitted PFD. Arrange a two-vehicle shuttle between McIver and Barton.

sections.notes: Usually 2–3 days. A free self-issued river permit is required. The Wenaha River comes in at Troy. Few roads, so plan your shuttle ahead.

rivers.blurb: Remote multi-day desert-canyon trips between Clarno and Cottonwood Bridge, with a shorter trip option at Thirtymile. Plan around river level, road access and year-round boating permits.

rivers.blurb: Canyon of Lodore, Whirlpool and Split Mountain canyons in Dinosaur National Monument. NPS permit required for every trip.

sections.notes: NPS multiday permit (lottery; $185 + $15 application). Starts in Colorado. NPS: 44 miles; 'Normal trip lengths are 4 days (3 nights) on the Green River' in high-use season. Gauge at Jensen is downstream of the Yampa confluence (Echo Park); Lodore Canyon flow is roughly the Greendale release.

guideTimes.conditions: Normal Green River high-use-season trip length in the 2025 NPS regulations: four days, three nights. This is a permitted itinerary, not hours afloat. Check current permit conditions.
guideTimes.sourceName: NPS Boating in the Monument, 2025 regulations

notices.title: Whitewater experience required
notices.text: NPS warns that rapids can reach Class IV depending on water level and that trip leaders and boat operators need experience on comparable rivers. The dotted line shows the general river corridor, not a route through individual rapids.

rivers.name: Green River (Flaming Gorge)
rivers.blurb: Dam-release tailwater below Flaming Gorge Dam through Red Canyon (Section A), to Browns Park (B) and on through Browns Park (C). Cold, clear water; PFDs required; no motors.

sections.notes: Section A. USFS: 7 miles, rapids class I and II. BLM: flotation tubes NOT recommended; PFDs required; flows fluctuate with dam releases (800-4500+ cfs).

guideTimes.conditions: Red Canyon Lodge describes about three hours travelling straight through the seven-mile Section A. This is approximate visitor guidance with no stated flow or craft-specific calibration; fishing and other stops can make the trip much longer.

rivers.blurb: Sand Island to Mexican Hat (Upper San Juan) and the Goosenecks / Mexican Hat to Clay Hills (Lower San Juan). BLM permit required year-round.

sections.notes: BLM permit required year-round (recreation.gov lottery). BLM trip planner: 27 miles, typically 2-3 days; river has class II to III rapids. River left (south) is Navajo Nation - separate permit to camp/hike. Do not leave vehicles overnight at Mexican Hat (break-ins).

rivers.name: Columbia River (Hanford Reach)
rivers.gaugeName: Columbia River below Priest Rapids Dam
rivers.blurb: The last free-flowing, non-tidal stretch of the U.S. Columbia — White Bluffs, Hanford's reactors, salmon and eagles.

sections.notes: Huge river with strong, swirling current and wind-driven waves. Coyote Rapids (Class II) can be avoided. The Hanford Site is closed: you may not get out of your boat and enter the reservation. Flows swing up to 10 ft quickly with Priest Rapids Dam operations. NPS lists ~19 mi; USFWS lists 18 mi. Discover Pass required to park at Vernita Bridge (WDFW-managed, per NPS). No camping at Vernita (WDFW).

rivers.name: Cowlitz River (below Mayfield Dam)
rivers.blurb: Big, dam-fed, easy river famous for salmon and steelhead — a fast, mellow float.

sections.notes: Busy fishing river — expect drift boats and anglers. Cold, powerful water. Both launches are run by Tacoma Power, which says there is no fee to use them (Blue Creek allows camping up to 3 days, no fires).
sections.mapPendingReason: Blue Creek (Cowlitz Trout Hatchery): Batch 1 (2026-10-25). Legal access is confirmed: Tacoma Power's Cowlitz Trout Hatchery page says Blue Creek Boat Launch (273 Blue Creek Lane, Toledo) gives free public river access, with 3-day camping in the lot. It gives an address only. No agency coordinate exists: WDFW's Facilities GIS has no ramp here, and its Blue Creek parking feature comment says it 'does not account for Tacoma Power's boat launch and assoc facilities'. The WDFW Blue Creek page is the ADA fishing-platform site. Imagery shows a ramp to the shore south of the lot near 46.4838, -122.7311, and boatlaunchmap/OSM give 46.48381, -122.73049, but neither is an agency source, and OSM maps a second unnamed ramp about 400 m upstream. Imagery (research/raw/batch4/bc19_g.png, z19): a paved lane from the trailer lot reaches the water (~46.48381,-122.73049, matching OSM), but OSM also maps a second ramp ~400 m upstream and no agency source says which one is Tacoma Power's. rivers.name: Grande Ronde River (Troy – Boggan's)
rivers.gaugeName: Grande Ronde River at Troy, OR
rivers.blurb: Remote basalt canyon in Washington's southeast corner below Troy, Oregon.

sections.notes: Long day. Take out at the public WDFW Boggans water-access site (unimproved ramp) at the SR 129 bridge; Boggan's Oasis next door is a private store that runs shuttles. The put-in is in Oregon, so Oregon boating rules apply until the river enters Washington. Oregon Waterway Access Permit required for non-motorized boats on the Oregon part of the river; since Jan 1, 2026 it applies to boats of any length ($6/7 days, $20/yr). WDFW Boggans take-out: Discover Pass or WDFW Vehicle Access Pass.

gaugeContext.note: USGS 05342000 measures the lower Kinni at County F. The reading provides river conditions; it does not measure travel speed, the dam-side launch, or St. Croix backwater and wind effects near the beach.

timing.note: No reviewed flow-to-speed calibration is assigned. The County F outfitter time is separate planning guidance; no live ETA or GPS time remaining is calculated.

rivers.blurb: The lower Kinni near River Falls: a popular gorge paddle below Powell Falls Dam to County F, with a longer option to the St. Croix beach. Expect moving water, rapids and hand-carried boats. This is the St. Croix tributary, separate from Milwaukee’s Kinnickinnic River.

sections.notes: A wooded gorge paddle with frequent riffles, rapids, sharp bends and fallen-tree hazards. Carry in below the dam and finish at County F. The local outfitter recommends intermediate to advanced paddlers; expect to maneuver or carry around obstacles. This is not a passive tubing itinerary.

sections.difficulty: Open-water lake crossing — challenging in wind and boat traffic
sections.notes: This trip continues from the Rock River into Lake Koshkonong and exits at Newville. The water-trail guide classifies the lake crossing as challenging because of its broad open water and motorboat traffic. Avoid high winds and approaching storms. Arrange a vehicle shuttle and plan for active paddling; river current alone does not determine the crossing time. The existing 11.7-mile planning distance is preliminary USGS geometry, not a surveyed or approved navigation route.

Expect fast water and boulders near the tailwater and changing wood obstacles. The 4.1-mile planning distance remains preliminary; it is not a surveyed route or a calibrated float-time estimate.

accessPoints.sourceName: USFWS Facilities/Property points (public view), 'White Bluffs Boat Ramp' (ObjectID 1215, asset 10004685, Public_Use 'Public Use', status Valid)
accessPoints.note: Batch 2. Coordinate is USFWS's own asset point for the ramp, separate from its 'White Bluffs Boat Ramp Parking' point (46.675380, -119.453112). Esri World Imagery (z19, checked 2026-10-25, research/raw/batch2/whitebluffs.png) puts it on the concrete ramp a few metres from the water's edge (the v1/OSM slipway point is ~11 m away). Legal access: USFWS Hanford Reach pages (https://www.fws.gov/national-monument/hanford-reach and .../visit-us/activities/boating---motorized) describe the concrete two-lane White Bluffs Boat Launch on the Wahluke Unit. It is CLOSED to launching motorized craft Nov 1-Jun 30 (waterfowl sanctuary), but loading/unloading non-motorized craft (canoes, kayaks, rafts) is allowed year-round, though you may have to carry boats to/from the parking lot. Monument is open sunrise to sunset; the launch is open 2 h before sunrise to 2 h after sunset for fishing entry (USFWS 2025 regulations brochure).
